samples.summary: Row/column reorder checks the whole post-move merge map for freeze straddling, so one pre-existing straddling block refuses every unrelated move forever
samples.evidence: `moveCells` builds `movedMerges = moveMergeMap(this.merges, ...)` and then refuses with `merge-move-frozen` if *any* entry in the resulting map crosses the freeze (lines 1606-1612) — not just the blocks the move relocates. `moveMerge`/`remapIndex` leave blocks outside the move untouched, so a block that already straddled before the move still straddles after it and trips the check. A straddling block is reachable: freeze and merges were independent before this change (so existing documents can hold one), and the diff's own tests seed exactly that state through the store (`packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts` "should snap the freeze past a straddling block after an insert") on the grounds that peers and the v1 API can produce it. In such a tab every drag-reorder of any row/column is silently refused with a misleading "Can't move a merged cell across a frozen row" notice, and it never self-heals (the snap only runs in `setFreezePane`/`shiftCells`). The same defect is duplicated server-side in `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-structure.controller.ts:194-203), which 409s every `POST move` on such a tab. Scoping the check to blocks whose position actually changes — or comparing against the pre-move straddle set, the way `moveRangeTo` scopes to `movedMerges` — is what the other paths do.

samples.summary: Backend move refusal inherits the same whole-map straddle check, 409ing unrelated moves on any tab that already holds a straddling merge
samples.evidence: `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` walks every entry of `moveMergeMap(...)` and throws `ConflictException` when any of them crosses the freeze, regardless of whether the move touched that block. A tab whose merge map already straddles the freeze (possible for any document created before this change, since `PUT freeze` and `PUT merges` were independent) therefore cannot use `POST .../move` at all, and the error message points at a block the caller never asked to move. Unlike `assertMoveKeepsMerges` (which is inherently about the moved range), this one has no relation to the requested move.

samples.summary: `PUT freeze` now calls `parseRef` on every stored merge key with no guard, so a malformed key turns a freeze write into an unhandled 500
samples.evidence: `snapFreezePastMerges` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/merging.ts:346-347) calls `parseRef(anchorSref)` on every key with no try/catch, and `parseRef` throws `Invalid Reference` for a key with no leading letters (coordinates.ts:350). `setFreeze` previously never read `ws.merges`; it now feeds the raw stored map in. `safeWorksheetRecordEntries` only handles duplicate-ownKeys, not key validity, and the merges field is a plain CRDT object that only `PUT merges` validates — which is precisely the threat model this same diff hardens against in `Sheet.rebuildMergeCoverMap` (sheet.ts:890-899, new try/catch + round-trip check). The engine-side `setFreezePane` is safe because it passes the already-cleaned `this.merges`; the backend path is not, and the throw escapes `doc.update` as a 500 on every freeze write for that tab.

samples.summary: The freeze snap can silently delete a user's freeze (release to 0) on an unrelated insert/delete, which the API contract does not admit
samples.evidence: `sweep` returns 0 whenever the snap would grow past `MaxSnappedFreeze` (`if (snapped !== line && snapped > MaxSnappedFreeze) return 0;`). That path is reached not only from an explicit `setFreezePane` but from `Sheet.shiftCells` (sheet.ts:1472) and `shiftWorksheetViewState` (worksheet-structure.ts:278), i.e. from any row/column insert or delete, including one issued through `POST insert`/`POST delete`. So an insert entirely unrelated to a large merged block can wipe the tab's freeze with no signal, and the controller doc explicitly tells callers only that the count may *grow* ("may leave the tab with more frozen rows or columns than it had"), so a client reading back `GET .../freeze` per that contract will not expect 0.

samples.summary: XLSX merge-budget accounting double-counts duplicate anchors, under-importing merges
samples.evidence: The loop keys `worksheet.merges[toSref(startRef)] = span`, so two `mergeCell` elements sharing a start ref overwrite one map entry, but the budget is incremented unconditionally (`entries: budget.entries + 1`, `coveredCells: + rowSpan*columnSpan`). A file with repeated or overlapping anchors therefore charges the budget for entries the map does not hold, and later legitimate merges in the same file are dropped by `mergeBudgetAdmits`.

samples.summary: Copy buffer is not revalidated when the copied range lies past axis-ID coverage, so a remote structural edit leaves a stale buffer that re-creates merges at wrong coordinates
samples.evidence: `revalidateCopyBuffer` returns immediately when `buffer.sourceAnchors` is undefined (sheet.ts:2315), and `anchorsForRange` returns undefined whenever either corner is past `getRowOrder()`/`getColOrder()` length (refToAnchor returns null for an index beyond the materialized axis). Copying cells below/right of materialized rows is ordinary (the grid is far larger than the CRDT axis order — see `rangeToRangeAnchor`'s comment at anchor-conversion.ts:90-95). For such a buffer a peer's row insert/reorder arrives as a reload, the buffer survives with stale indices, and a subsequent internal paste now relocates formulas *and re-creates merged blocks* from those stale coordinates — the exact failure the new clearing/revalidation was added to prevent. Falling back to clearing the buffer on any structural reload would close it.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. sheet.ts:1606-1612 iterates the entire post-move merge map (moveMergeMap over this.merges) and refuses with 'merge-move-frozen' if ANY block crosses the freeze, not only relocated blocks. merging.ts:218-291 confirms moveMerge/moveMergeMap leave blocks outside the moved band (and all row coordinates on a column move) unchanged, so a pre-existing straddling block still straddles post-move and trips the check, blocking unrelated reorders. The straddling precondition is reachable: loadMerges (sheet.ts:588) and loadFreezePane (sheet.ts:564) apply no snap, snapping exists only in setFreezePane (sheet.ts:544) and shiftCells (sheet.ts:1472), and the repo's own tests seed this state through the store (merge.test.ts:1051-1063, 1078, 1097) citing peers/v1 API as producers. moveRows/moveColumns (sheet.ts:1370-1380) reach moveCells with no pre-snap, so no guard makes it unreachable. The same over-broad check is duplicated server-side at worksheet-structure.controller.ts:181-204, 409ing every POST move on such a tab. By contrast moveRangeTo (sheet.ts:2901-2927) correctly scopes to getMergesIntersecting(source). Real, reachable, misleading refusal of a normal-use gesture: major correctness defect.

finding.summary: The freeze snap is unbounded, so a tall/wide merged block can set frozenRows/Cols to a value the renderer paints row-by-row every frame
finding.evidence: `setFreezePane` now stores `snapFreezePastMerges(...)` with no ceiling on the result. The merge budget permits a single span of `MaxMergedCells = 100000` cells (e.g. `rs: 100000, cs: 1`), so freezing row 1 under such a block snaps `frozenRows` to 100000. `GridCanvas.render` then calls `renderQuadrantCells(ctx, 1, fr + 1, ...)` for quadrants A and B (gridcanvas.ts:329-352, 400-403), and `buildRenderableRefs(rowStart, rowEnd, ...)` materializes one ref per frozen cell — the clip rect does not bound the loop. That is exactly the pathology `parseFreeze`'s own doc comment describes ("an out-of-grid freeze allocates per frame and the UI never paints — which also means the user cannot reach the freeze menu to undo it"), now reachable from a normal editor gesture (freeze 1 row) and from `PUT freeze` with a modest `rows` value. `snapFreezePastMerges` should clamp, or the gesture should be refused rather than snapped, past some bound.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts `snapFreezePastMerges` applies "no ceiling on the result", letting a 100,000-row merged block snap `frozenRows` to 100000. The sweep in merging.ts:350-363 ends with `if (snapped !== line && snapped > MaxSnappedFreeze) return 0;`, with `MaxSnappedFreeze = 1000` (merging.ts:60). Growth beyond the ceiling releases the axis to 0 rather than storing an unpaintable boundary, and the constant's own doc (merging.ts:44-59) names the exact GridCanvas per-frame pathology the reviewer says is unhandled. All three writers go through this function: Sheet.setFreezePane (sheet.ts:543-548), the shift path (sheet.ts:1472), and the backend PUT freeze (worksheet.controller.ts:121-128). Tests assert the claimed scenario yields {frozenRows: 0, frozenCols: 0} for a block of rs = MaxSnappedFreeze + 2 frozen at row 1 (merge.test.ts:983-995), the column-axis equivalent (merge.test.ts:1023-1031), and that a block inside the ceiling still snaps (merge.test.ts:998-1008). The only pass-through case is a boundary the caller requested that nothing straddles (merge.test.ts:1011-1021), delegated by design to parseFreeze (worksheet-settings.ts:50-64) — that is not the merge-driven trigger the finding describes. The remediation the finding requests ("snapFreezePastMerges should clamp") is already implemented at the cited line.
